correctness.rationale: For finite positive weights w_i, coordinate-sign translation operators are still isometries of pointed Lip_0, so averaging any projection yields the canonical Walsh projection Q_A as unique character-diagonal equivariant projector, proving minimum norm. Weighted Lipschitz norm is maximum over edge differences/w_i. Fourier derivative along i is convolution by K_i, yielding norm <=max_i c_i where c_i is the mean absolute coordinate-shadow Walsh kernel. Pick i with smallest weight and let h=sign K_i; f=(w_i/2) x_i h(x_without_i), normalized at basepoint, has Lipschitz norm 1 because every transverse edge has weight at least w_i and its amplitude difference <=w_i. Its i-th projected derivative attains c_i. Coordinate-transitive spectral support makes every c_i identical, so sharp weighted norm is the unweighted coordinate-shadow constant. The homogeneous layer count follows by binomial signs; degree-2 formula gives n=4 value 3/2 for every positive w. Zero-kernel signs, n>=2, degree 1 and n endpoints are accounted for; argument proves all weights, not only tested rational examples.
